design.title: Within-place variance penalty: each member's pooled feature of one place, standardised against its spread across places, must be the same in all three surveys
design.eli5: Each of the drone's two navigators boils a photo down to a short description of the place it is looking at - 112 numbers. We checked what happens to that description when the SAME spot is shown in two of the training photographs taken in different years: it changes by about a third of the amount it would change if you showed a completely different place, and most of that change is season and shadow, not geography. So the navigators have partly been describing the photograph rather than the ground, and a brand-new photograph gets a description that matches nowhere. The fix is a rule during training: every time a spot is shown in all three photographs at once, the three descriptions must come out the same, judged against how much descriptions differ between places. Whatever in a description tracks the time of year gets squeezed out; whatever tracks the streets and buildings stays. Nothing the drone carries changes - only what it was taught to pay attention to.
design.hypothesis: The held-out 2024 photograph's usable-fix rate has sat at 7-12.5% through seven designs because the deployed feature of a place still changes with the survey, and no experiment has yet actually forbidden that. Experiment 3 tried (cosine between L2-normalised GAP features of the same position in different surveys) and was reverted, but a design-stage probe on the current champion's exported graph shows its metric could never have bitten: the RAW cosine between the pooled features of two DIFFERENT places is 0.70 (runs/_probe_exp9_wpv.py, 400 lattice positions, three TRAINING captures only, truedop_2024 never opened), because post-ReLU average-pooled features share a large positive common component. A same-place cross-survey cosine of 0.966 at epoch 1 and 0.935 at the end therefore meant 'the features are post-ReLU', not 'the three surveys agree' - and experiment 6 dismissed feature invariance on exactly that misreading ('the three training appearances were mapped to nearly the same vector'). Measured properly, with the batch mean removed, the champion's same-place cross-survey cosine is 0.69 and different-place is 0.00; as a within-place variance fraction of the per-dimension standardised feature (0 = identical feature in all surveys, 1 = a survey change moves the feature as far as a change of place), the three training surveys read 0.295, versus 0.152 for two independent draws of the photometric augmentation on one survey - the kept exposure/sharpness randomisation (exp 4) covers only half of what a change of survey does to the feature, and nothing in the training signal addresses the other half. The consequence is visible in the same probe: the SAME member, shown the SAME place at the SAME heading in two training surveys, names the same cell only 28-40% of the time (per-survey top1 34-46%), so even on photographs it trained on, the committee's agreement gate is largely gating survey-driven feature drift, not place knowledge; on a fourth survey the drift is at least as large and the cell beliefs land elsewhere. The remedy is the library's L2 rank-1 mechanism (cross-survey latent consistency, SSL4EO's top rung) implemented so that it cannot be satisfied for free: standardise every dimension of each member's 112-d pooled feature over the mini-batch (zero mean, unit variance), then penalise the variance that remains WITHIN a position across its three surveys' views, scaled so unrelated views read 1.0. Standardisation per dimension means a feature dimension that mostly encodes survey state (canopy greenness, shadow strength, colour pipeline) has within-place variance near its total variance and is penalised hardest, while a dimension that encodes place is nearly free - the trunk is pushed, over 218k paired views per epoch and all 2,970 places at once, to discard the directions along which the three surveys differ and keep the ones along which places differ. That is the domain-generalisation bet of this era stated as a loss: the fourth survey's deviations (season, sun angle, cars, pipeline) are assumed to lie largely in the span of the deviations between a summer standard DOP, a leaf-off true-ortho and an early-spring true-ortho, and a feature made invariant to that span transfers. No projector (a projector would let the deployed feature keep survey content and discard it only downstream, the opposite of what the linear cell head needs), no stop-gradient (the batch standard deviation in the denominator carries gradient on purpose: it is VICReg's variance term in disguise, and the 2,970-way cross-entropy on the same vector makes collapse impossible). It is one loss term on the existing committee; the exported graph is byte-identical.
